name: Gadolinium
summary: Representative of the lanthanides: many coupled degrees of freedom in the 4f shell, but slow and energy-intensive actuation. In the schema it shows the case of a high number of variables with poor actuation, and with the magnetocaloric effect it provides a coupling from spin to temperature.

degrees_of_freedom.description: 4f7 configuration, S = 7/2, largest magnetic moment of all elements in the ground state

couplings.source: Dan'kov et al., Phys. Rev. B 57, 3478 (1998); saturation moment 7.55 mu_B per atom

validity.condition: near the Curie temperature of 293 K

couplings.source: Dan'kov, Tishin, Pecharsky & Gschneidner, Phys. Rev. B 57, 3478 (1998), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.57.3478
couplings.notes: Linear approximation. In reality the entropy change scales roughly with H^(2/3); the gain is chosen so that at 5 T it matches the measured -10 J/(kg*K).

validity.condition: adiabatic condition, dT = -T/c_p * dS with T = 293 K and c_p = 236 J/(kg*K); yields 12.5 K at 5 T

couplings.source: Dan'kov et al., Phys. Rev. B 57, 3478 (1998)
couplings.notes: Coupling from spin to temperature. Together with c_temp_mag it forms a cycle and is the physical basis of magnetic cooling.

couplings.source: Curie temperature 293 K, unusually close to room temperature

feedback_loops.notes: The field lowers the magnetic entropy, the material warms up, and the higher temperature lowers the magnetization. Self-limiting, and usable as a cooling cycle for exactly that reason.

gaps: The magnetocaloric effect depends strongly on the temperature window; the linear approximations hold only near 293 K.
The 4f degrees of freedom beyond the total magnetization (orbital occupation, crystal field levels) are not represented in the schema, because no practical actuator exists for them.
Pecharsky & Gschneidner 1997 was listed as a source in v0.1, but it treats Gd5Si2Ge2 and not pure gadolinium. Replaced by Dan'kov et al. 1998.
sources: Dan'kov, Tishin, Pecharsky & Gschneidner, Phys. Rev. B 57, 3478 (1998), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.57.3478
Pecharsky & Gschneidner, Phys. Rev. Lett. 78, 4494 (1997), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.4494 - concerns Gd5Si2Ge2, not pure Gd
